to be honest: used when you say what you really think
To be honest, I didn't like the film.
to be sick and tired: to be very bored or annoyed with something
I'm sick and tired of this rain.
to face something: to deal with a difficult situation
You need to face your fears.
to lack something: to not have something, or not have enough
to no avail: We tried to help, but to no avail.
to rage quit: to stop playing a game suddenly because you are angry
He rage quit after losing five times.
to shop for: to go to buy a particular thing
We need to shop for a new sofa.
tornado: a very strong wind that moves in a circle
tour: We went on a tour of the city.
tourism: the business of providing holidays for tourists
Tourism is important for the economy.
tourist: a person who travels for pleasure
The city is full of tourists in summer.
tourist office: an office that gives information to tourists
Ask at the tourist office for a map.
towel: a piece of cloth for drying your body
Can I have a clean towel?
tower block: a very tall building with many flats
She lives on the 15th floor of a tower block.
tradition: a custom that people have followed for a long time
It's a family tradition to eat together on Sundays.
traffic: the cars and other vehicles on a road
There was heavy traffic this morning.
training: the process of practising a sport or learning a job
trampoline: equipment for jumping up and down on
transport: ways of travelling, like buses and trains
travel: to go from one place to another, often far
treadmill: an exercise machine for walking or running in one place
I walk on the treadmill for 30 minutes.
trouble: I had trouble finding the house.
trunk: the space at the back of a car for bags (American English)
Put the bags in the trunk.
turn around: to move your body to face the other way
Turn around and look behind you.
turn out: to happen in a way you did not expect
The party turned out to be fun.
tuvalu: a small island country in the Pacific Ocean
Tuvalu is one of the smallest countries in the world.
tv host: a person who presents a TV programme
She works as a TV host.
tv series: a set of TV episodes with the same characters
We're watching a new TV series.
twig: a very small thin branch of a tree
The bird built a nest from twigs.
type in: to write something on a keyboard
typo: There's a typo in your email.
unbalance: An unbalance in the wheels makes the car shake.
uncertain: I'm uncertain about what to do.
uncertainty: a situation when things are not sure or known
There's a lot of uncertainty about the future.
unconscious: not awake because of an injury or illness
He was unconscious after the accident.
underdeveloped: not having modern industry or services
unease: a feeling of worry or discomfort
There was a sense of unease in the room.
unique: different from everything else; the only one of its kind
unripe: not ready to eat because it has not grown enough
urbanization: the process of towns and cities growing bigger
Urbanization changes the way people live.
usual: I'll meet you at the usual place.
vacuum: to clean with a machine that sucks up dirt
I vacuum the carpet every week.
value: how important or useful something is
vest: a piece of clothing without sleeves
He wore a white vest under his shirt.
view: what you can see from a place
The room has a beautiful view of the sea.
visa: an official document that lets you enter a country
Do I need a visa to visit the USA?
vision: an idea of how the future should be
The company has a clear vision.
visit: to go to see a person or place
vivid: very bright; very clear in your mind
I have vivid memories of my childhood.
voltage: the force of an electric current, measured in volts
Check the voltage before connecting it.
volunteer: a person who works without pay to help others
She works as a volunteer at the hospital.
vote: to choose someone or something in an election
vulnerability: a weakness that can be attacked or hurt
Hackers used a vulnerability in the system.
wait: Wait for me at the bus stop.
want: to wish to have or do something
I want a cup of tea.
wash: I need to wash my car.
washing machine: Put the towels in the washing machine.
way: a route; also how you do something
Is this the way to the station?
we can modernize those modules as we wan: a sentence saying the modules can be updated in any way you like
we were supposed to meet on friday but m: a sentence about moving a planned meeting to another day
weakness: a bad quality or part of someone or something
My biggest weakness is that I'm impatient.
wedding: a ceremony when two people get married
They invited 100 guests to the wedding.
weigh: to have a particular heaviness; to measure how heavy something is
weight: how heavy someone or something is
well-paid: He has a well-paid job in a bank.
west: the direction where the sun goes down
The sun sets in the west.
what exactly: used to ask for more detailed information
what have you been up to?: used to ask what someone has been doing recently
Hi! What have you been up to?
what's the use of?: used to ask why someone would do something useless
when you face difficulties: a phrase about the moment you meet problems
Stay calm when you face difficulties.
why don't we..?: used to suggest doing something together
Why don't we go to the beach?
will be able to: You will be able to see the sea from the room.
win: to be the best in a game or competition
wind: The wind blew my hat off.
windy: It's too windy to go sailing.
withdrawal: taking money out of a bank account
The cash machine charges a fee for each withdrawal.
women-only class: a sports lesson that only women can join
The gym offers a women-only class.
wonder: I wonder what time it is.
work ethics: beliefs about how hard and well people should work
She has a strong work ethic.
worry: to think a lot about problems or bad things that could happen
Don't worry, everything will be fine.
worse: The weather is worse today than yesterday.
would prefer: to like one thing more than another (polite)
would rather (not): to want to do one thing more than another
I would rather stay at home tonight.
would you rather ...?: used to ask what someone prefers
Would you rather have tea or coffee?
written: There is a written test and an oral test.
young adults: people between about 18 and 25 years old
The course is for young adults.
yummies: The kids ate all the yummies.
zest: great energy and enthusiasm; also something that makes things interesting
She has a zest for life.
